## Decisions

- Keep WGPU 29.0.3; inject one explicit GPU context for scenes and presentation.
- Text: Parley 0.9 layout/fallback/bidi plus required Swash 0.2.10 glyph images. The local Parley dictionary-analysis patch and test scope are documented in `vendor/parley/ELDIRON-PATCH.md`. These are already available in the local registry; version compatibility will be compiled and checked.
- Paths: Lyon tessellation with GPU rasterization; static Zeno masks remain only an optional asset/reference path. Coverage/AA quality remains a visual verification gate.
- Preserve serialized legacy core values through identity-compatible re-exports; new CPU image data has size/pixels without UI position/display scale.
- User instruction (2026-11-14): older experimental paint algorithm versions do not require backwards compatibility. Preserve current paint/project serialization; do not add legacy paint replay requirements to native producers.

## UI and host checkpoint (2026-11-11)

The paint foundation now drives real TheFramework UI trees through an application-owned WGPU host. This remains an intermediate implementation checkpoint; Creator and client entry points have not switched, and the full rewrite Goal remains active.

Implemented:

- `platform::{GpuApplication,UiSession,GpuPresenter}` separates application/UI state from device/surface ownership. `platform::winit` creates and presents a native WGPU window directly, supports asynchronous browser startup, resize/density changes, suspension and replacement generations, and rebuild callbacks. There is no destination-pixel callback in this contract.
- The same `GpuPresenter` accepts Rust surfaces created over a host-retained CAMetalLayer. The native test actually submitted and presented UI/text through this path without Winit.
- Neutral physical-key, committed-text, preedit, pointer, relative-motion, scroll, focus and file-drop events; explicit consumption separate from redraw; focused-widget undo/clipboard routing. Layout records screen transforms for inverse input mapping, including captured drags and scrolled/embedded controls.
- Canvas trees and converted scrolling/tree/stack/tab/split layouts emit ordered paint instead of composing raster caches. GPU layout retains dimensions without allocating pixel storage. A constraint-aware measurement hook lets wrapped tree text use actual shaping widths.
- Standard buttons, bars, separators, menus, labels, checkboxes, sliders, tabs, list/tree rows, dropdowns/popups, scrollbars, image views and GPU-image render views have explicit paint methods. New paint/preparation methods preserve existing controllers, IDs and authoring/event semantics. Unsupported families return an error; there is no raster fallback behind the new interface.
- Single/multiline editors share Parley layout for GPU glyph runs, selections, caret geometry and grapheme hit testing. Atomic committed text produces one undo entry; transient composition does not alter the document. Syntax foreground, matches/errors, line numbers, scrollbars and debugging backgrounds have GPU paint paths. Drag labels now use paint and Swash text rather than an intermediate text bitmap.
- File pickers are neutral queued requests. The desktop host adapter uses optional desktop dialogs; the shared UI no longer requires unsupported desktop dialog/clipboard dependencies on iOS. Foreign hosts can service requests and report completion.
- Added explicit device-loss tracking to the shared GPU context; application/UI state is retained outside the presenter.

### Startup/structural invalidation follow-up

An additional real-window geometry assertion caught a regression introduced when preinput geometry preparation was added: input arriving before GPU/application readiness could resize an empty canvas, then a later `set_layout` did not invalidate dimensions. The original presentation-only smoke check still submitted frames but did not detect empty child geometry.

Corrected the host ordering (input/resume callbacks wait for initialization), added canvas structural invalidation for installed widgets/layouts/child canvases, and included UI tree invalidation in host redraw decisions. Zero-size/absent targets no longer schedule rapid retry redraws. The regression fixture installs and replaces a layout at an unchanged size, verifies nonzero child geometry, and checks that a repaint is requested. The strengthened native smoke fixture verifies both widgets have nonzero assigned rectangles on every presented frame (11 paint operations). Six UI tests including actual CAMetalLayer presentation, all 88 framework library tests, and the native smoke run passed. Logs: `/private/tmp/eldiron-native-geometry-test.log`, `/private/tmp/eldiron-native-geometry-check.log`.

### RGBA/tile view conversion

`TheRGBAView` now emits an uploaded source-image blit plus GPU overlays for zoom/centering/scrolling, rectangular grids, sparse used/hover/drop cells, connected selection boundaries, icon selection, translucent paste previews, and anchor guides. Source and preview dirty flags are distinct from display invalidation, so moving/changing a selection does not upload the source image again. Sparse overlays iterate their state rather than every source cell when zoomed far out. Editable pixel storage remains an explicit source asset.

Validation: native GPU assertions check rectangular grid geometry, preservation of shared selection edges, paste opacity, no source upload on selection changes, and exactly one source-asset upload after a pixel edit. Seven UI integration tests (six actual GPU tests and one layout regression), the paint integration, and all 88 framework library tests passed; all four application compile checks passed. Logs: `/private/tmp/eldiron-tile-checkpoint-tests.log`, `/private/tmp/eldiron-tile-checkpoint-apps.log`. `native-wgpu-evidence/tiles-foundation.png` was captured and visually inspected. Overall rewrite remains active; remaining widget families and application/runtime migration continue.

### Rich text and Markdown

A shared text viewport planner now supplies scroll geometry for multiline editing, rich text and Markdown. Preparation receives an immutable theme explicitly, so theme-dependent text styles and code-highlight themes resolve before layout/paint rather than rebuilding layout from inside painting. Widget paint still accesses no GPU/device/registry; image requests remain behind the backend service.

### Procedural controls, collections and node canvas

Converted the remaining active built-in widget implementations: switch/time controls, icon grid and scrollable row, color/direction pickers, SDF view and node canvas. Layouts invoke a shared widget entry point that skips unassigned rectangles, preventing controls from drawing stray geometry at the origin. Collection preparation computes visible hit rectangles; image content invalidation is independent of hover/selection/scrolling.

The backend-neutral paint contract now includes colored triangle meshes with explicit sRGB interpolation, analytic nearest-distance fields/materials, and explicit repeating image sampling. The color picker emits a geometric hue ring and triangle; direction paint uses its own widget center. SDF views send analytic shapes/materials, preserving nearest-shape overlap rather than replacing it with painter-order fills. Fixed pre-existing signed-distance errors in rhombus/rectangular interiors and a zero-length direction normalization case. Analytic fields composite premultiplied linear color with density-aware edge coverage.

The node canvas retains interaction rectangles and emits node chrome, Swash labels, sockets, curves, cut feedback and focus through commands. Its command path clears legacy viewport pixel storage. CPU previews/overlays remain explicit source assets; GPU previews can be supplied as opaque image handles without UI/device coupling. Repeated overlays use one quad regardless of tile size. Preview/overlay content dirtiness is separate from interaction redraw. Hit testing honors the selected node's actual topmost draw order; deletion clears the stale selected index and preserves/remaps GPU preview handles. Application preview producers still need migration to the GPU handle API, and legacy wire cutting still needs its hit geometry reconciled with the painted curve.

Validation passed: 91 library tests, three renderer-free command UI tests, paint GPU integration and twelve UI integration tests (eleven actual GPU fixtures plus one structural-layout regression). New fixtures verify visible icon selection after scrolling, one-thumbnail invalidation, no upload on selection, unassigned-widget suppression, time-track agreement, actual color-ring/SDF GPU pixels, nearest-material overlap, zero procedural raster-asset uploads, live GPU-only node previews, one-quad tiled overlays, exactly one terminal-connection event and node-drag event. Procedural and node captures were visually inspected at 150% density. All four application compatibility checks, browser host compile and iOS-simulator UI/presenter compile passed. Logs: `/private/tmp/eldiron-icon-headless-tests.log`, `/private/tmp/eldiron-widget-checkpoint-tests.log`, `/private/tmp/eldiron-widget-checkpoint-{apps,web,ios}.log`. Evidence: `native-wgpu-evidence/procedural-controls.png`, `native-wgpu-evidence/node-canvas.png`.

A first GPU shader run rejected a reserved WGSL identifier; it was renamed and the complete GPU regression suite then passed. A direction-line pixel assertion was adjusted to account for fractional-DPI MSAA coverage; logical geometry and visible pixel darkness are both verified. These are intermediate checks; full Creator/client migration, performance and platform acceptance remain outstanding, and the overall Goal stays active.

### CPU session, schema boundary and terminal adoption

Added `eldiron-runtime::GameSession`: it owns project/engine assets/server/current map, an elapsed-time-driven clock and one collector for region messages, speech, choices, audio requests, world text and container requests. Render rate does not advance simulation. Bounded catch-up retains debt; paused sessions clear elapsed wall time. A host selects output channels and takes pending region events once. Started-session shutdown belongs to the session owner; constructing/dropping an unstarted session does not clear engine state.

The terminal now owns a `GameSession` and uses its startup/tick/output APIs. Removed its duplicate content preparation, character/item/template startup, local-player setup and server-update loop. Terminal text/roguelike/AI presentation remains its own controller. ### Application-owned scene views and GPU domains

Created `eldiron-presentation::SceneViews`. Each stable view ID retains its own injected `SceneHandler`/SceneVM, camera/uniform/history state and GPU target, while views share an atlas. The manager binds to the host registry/device domain; it never owns a window or simulation clock. Outputs carry opaque image handles, descriptors, output revisions and caller content revisions. Unchanged outputs/handles are reused; zero-sized views suspend; resize/removal invalidates replaced registrations. Explicit captures return revision-stamped readback tickets. Applications must call `remove`/`clear` when releasing views while retaining the registry.

`SceneHandler::with_vm` enables application injection without initializing a compatibility GPU. SceneRenderTarget now retains one stable GPU image lease rather than constructing a new wrapper every render. Added explicit context generations to injected SceneVM state and VM layers; target/state domain mismatches are rejected before submission. Legacy constructor paths do not satisfy the new injected `render_gpu` ownership contract.

The replacement-device test exposed a real ownership bug: WGPU 29's core device equality proxy compares its device ID, which can coincide between separate WGPU instances. A device-equality-based atlas/cache check reused a texture from the wrong instance and failed during bind-group creation. The canonical path now tags atlas/texture resources with renderkit's explicit generation, recreates GPU atlas storage from retained CPU sources when that generation changes, and keeps mip pipelines with their texture resources. Removed the thread-global mip-pipeline cache. Legacy raw-device APIs remain compatibility paths pending retirement.

Stronger residency checks also found that intermediate VM layer and ping-pong textures still allocated CPU pixel vectors even though the final SceneRenderTarget did not. Those renderer-owned intermediates now use GPU-only storage too. Explicit legacy capture remains an opt-in CPU consumer. Fixed atlas packing/metadata preparation order so a newly supplied shared atlas has valid tile indices before the first geometry build; atlas layout changes invalidate dependent geometry.

Validation passed: two actual GPU scene-view fixtures compose independently transformed textured views, verify shared atlas identity, stable output/image leases, idle reuse, zero CPU layer/history storage, ping-pong targets, suspend/resume, resizing, retained capture revisions, removal and foreign registry/context rejection. A second fixture reuses CPU atlas sources across separately created GPU contexts and successfully renders on the replacement domain. SceneVM's independent-output GPU fixture, framework 91 library tests, paint GPU integration and twelve UI integration tests passed after these changes. Four-application compatibility compilation passed. Browser and iOS-simulator presentation compilation passed. Logs: `/private/tmp/eldiron-view-checkpoint-{gpu,scenevm,ui,apps,web,ios}.log`.

This remains a scene ownership/composition checkpoint. Game-screen/HUD presentation and actual Creator/client adoption continue next. The new crate does not yet move the legacy aggregate Rusterix/controller outward or eliminate the legacy shared graphical startup bridges. Opaque raster-2D view pixels/transforms are verified; transparent scene-output color/alpha normalization, 3D/isometric application parity, shared geometry-buffer ownership, picking/async revisions, complete application recovery, resource budgets and release performance remain work. No M1/M5/M6 completion claim; overall Goal remains active.

### Avatar/profile/item source preparation and native silhouettes

Implemented a CPU source-preparation boundary rather than drawing actor/item artwork into a UI-sized bitmap. `rusterix::client::content` describes avatar/profile/item source recipes, appearance fingerprints and source fitting policy. `presentation::screen::ContentSources` owns bounded source storage, negative lookup caching, immutable source leases and explicit asset/publication revisions. Palette/material/avatar/artwork edits, project replacement and asynchronously published appearance variants must advance `ContentRevision`; GPU/device replacement alone does not invalidate CPU source data. Outstanding leases remain usable after eviction. Cache byte counts describe cache-owned storage, not externally retained leases.

- Source generation is independent of widget dimensions, crop, text and health/movement. Profile alpha bounds are prepared once; face/bust/full crops become UV geometry, without copying/scaling a destination bitmap. Authored portraits remain uncropped. Conservative recipe fingerprints and raw requested animation phases still need tightening during the resource/performance gate; unrelated equipment metadata can cause extra regeneration.
- Existing item icon drawing and native preparation now share source selection, including project overrides, explicit animated tiles, item source bindings, rules artwork and generated fallback assets. Removed four obsolete CPU drawing helpers. Source-sized procedural image generation remains an explicit asset preparation operation; quantity badges and fitting are presentation work.
- `ScreenImages::rgba_versioned` avoids hashing immutable prepared image bytes on each paint. Prepared source identities are unique for their immutable lease; changed content gets a new identity. Unversioned mutable/editor sources retain byte fingerprint validation. GPU source cache owner/frame/retirement rules are unchanged.
- Shared profile layout projects identity, stat bars, selected frame and image geometry. `ProfileLayout` retains Parley shaping and reflows using actual shaped identity heights, invalidating on font revision/content/size changes. Source crop/size/stat changes do not rebuild glyph layouts or the source artwork. Painting reads prepared geometry/runs and uses Swash atlas blits.
- Added generic GPU `ImageOutline` alpha dilation for avatar/profile silhouettes. Sampling outside the UV crop is transparent; outline width follows local logical coordinates through density/transforms and is clipped by the owning widget. Linear premultiplied composition preserves alpha coverage. The kernel skips opaque interiors and stops sampling at full coverage. Broad outlines still have radius-dependent cost; this is not a completed performance gate.
- Damage flash timing/color remains controller-owned and separate from source preparation. Binding a different party member resets the health baseline instead of flashing because two actors have different health.

Added `eldiron_presentation::GameScreenController` consuming borrowed `RuntimeView`, shared `ScreenElements`, addressed batches, prepared artwork and host-supplied scene/image services. It owns no server, clock, surface or destination framebuffer. The presentation crate now depends on runtime in the planned direction; there is no reverse dependency through shared/Rusterix. This remains a rendering/preparation integration checkpoint: native event routing, complete HUD families, region fallback/launcher assembly and canonical cutover are not complete.

- Separate `receive` queues each explicit addressed batch once; repeated preparation/paint does not drain/requeue authoritative messages. Audio/world-text/container consumers can receive the same application-distributed batch separately.
- Preparation retains message/profile geometry, source-art leases, CPU screen geometry and stable per-widget view identities. Hidden message/source/view work is skipped. GPU game views are injected into the caller's `SceneViews`/registry, configured from the same CPU world/config and released explicitly before closing/replacing a screen while retaining that registry.
- Native composition covers current game/text/avatar/profile/stat/message/input/button/choice/decorative paint adapters, source-sized portraits/items, static base/foreground textured triangles and independent GPU game images. Base composition uses intersected vector stencil clips outside game rectangles, preserving the existing negative-decoration layering without CPU hole-punch buffers, display-sized mask assets or scene readback.
- Shared command-slot, placeholder, party selection, visibility and button-state policies moved from aggregate Client into `screen_model::bindings`; existing client/world-text/intent-cursor callers consume those policies too.
- `GameFonts` owns one project-scoped Parley registry across screen navigation. Each screen borrows it for layout/paint. It checks authored font bytes only on content revisions, removes deleted project families on rebuild, and invalidates every screen through an explicit owner/revision identity. Unchanged assets and screen navigation preserve font blob IDs and Swash GPU cache reuse. Creator chrome keeps a separate font registry; Parley blob IDs are globally unique (verified in pinned `linebender_resource_handle` source), so both can use a host's glyph cache without aliasing named project fonts.
- Explicit portrait recipes cache animated source artwork independently of actor health/display-name changes. Source-frame normalization, conservative item metadata fingerprints, broad-outline kernel cost and whole-application resource/performance gates remain outstanding.

### Neutral input and shared editor-state extraction

Moved cursor/selection/text-edit data and operations out of `theui::thewidget::thetextedit` into renderer-independent `theframework::text_edit`. Focused tests reproduced three pre-existing Unicode defects in the extracted state, then verified fixes shared by existing widgets: multiline copy sliced the last row using a grapheme position as a UTF-8 byte offset; deletion of trailing spaces could slice inside a multibyte character; commits joining an existing grapheme could advance the cursor beyond the resulting row. Insertion now derives the caret from the resulting grapheme boundary, and copying/indent-selection/deletion use grapheme-aware ranges. Cursor/selection/row serialization is unchanged.

## Native editing engine and authored input checkpoint (2026-11-11)

Added a renderer-independent `EditorController` around the pinned Parley plain editor, plus an `EditorView` for logical viewport geometry and paint commands. Text layout, visual bidi navigation, pointer/word/logical-line selection, caret/selection/preedit geometry and platform candidate rectangles now derive from the same Parley layout. The controller has no widgets, window, GPU or system clipboard dependency; the existing serialized row/cursor/selection types retain their compatibility format.

The controller separates physical commands from committed text, keeps IME replacement transient until commit, restores selected content on cancellation/blur and records composition as one undo transaction. Undo/redo storage is bounded at 8 MiB per editor. Clipboard reads/writes are explicit requests; cuts delete only after a successful write, and completion requires matching content, selection, focus and a process-unique request token. Tokens cannot alias after screen/editor replacement. Forward/backward deletion consumes extended graphemes, including combining sequences, emoji and CRLF. Single-line filtering also maps preedit byte indices through removed control characters. Font owner/revision changes invalidate retained glyph snapshots; selection-only changes and identical paints reuse them.

The view handles pointer drag selection, scrolling, page navigation, focus, viewport clipping, selection/preedit/caret paint and IME coordinates in logical host units. Trailing spaces participate in horizontal scroll extent. Repeated preparation preserves user scrollback until the caret moves or layout changes. The host owns blink timing, clipboard fulfillment, outer transforms and physical-density conversion; the adapter exposes these requirements rather than creating a window or drawing a bitmap.

Native `GameScreenController` inputs now retain these editors, publish committed text into existing UI bindings, traverse visible fields in stable authored-ID order, release focus on submit/cancel/window blur and reject callbacks for hidden or unfocused fields. IME preview never mutates the widget value or binding. The stateless screen-paint preview uses the same paint adapter. The prior underscore placeholder is removed from the native screen path. Legacy Creator/framework editor widgets still use their old editing adapters; their migration and complete native screen/world routing remain required.

## Shared choice controller checkpoint (2026-11-11)

Moved dropdown/tab capture and pending selection out of the aggregate legacy client into `screen_model::ChoiceController`. ## Native player application checkpoint (2026-11-11)

The client library now assembles `PlayerApplication` from the shared CPU `PlayerSession`, retained `GameScreenController`/`GameFonts`, and a separate presenter-bound owner of `SceneViews`/`ScreenImageCache`. The graphical session queues startup actions until acknowledgement, collapses consecutive movement states, preserves one-shot order and bounds the queue with an explicit error. `GameSession::view_region` lets output services resolve each addressed batch against its own region. All region batches are drained once before the host services consume audio/world-text/container output.

## Shared native transcript editor checkpoint (2026-11-11)

Authored fields and transcript command lines now share one `ScreenTextTarget` focus owner and retained Parley `EditorView`s. ## Addressed text input and presentation lifecycle checkpoint (2026-11-12)

`HostContext` now exposes a `TextInputState` containing both logical candidate geometry and a process-unique `TextInputTarget`. Shared editor controllers retain their target through ordinary edits, layout/font/DPI changes and GPU recreation, and invalidate it on blur, external document replacement or recreation. Native callbacks use addressed `TextFor`/`CompositionFor` events. Both the screen router and editor reject events for another target, including an old callback after refocusing the same authored field. The legacy TheUI adapter also rejects callbacks from previous focus tokens; full document-replacement epochs for its old widgets still depend on adopting the common editor controllers.

A platform-neutral `ImeSession` pins preedit/commit to the originating target until the native input-session boundary. Winit resets IME when the target changes and snapshots the target before a physical key is dispatched, preventing an activation key from becoming text in the editor it just opened. Foreign wrappers can round-trip the same opaque 64-bit token. The foreign Metal fixture verifies that replacing a surface/device preserves the active editor token and content. Live OS keyboard/IME validation is unavailable because the Mac is locked; the attempted CUA inventory explicitly reported that condition. The temporary input test process was closed without changing lock/security settings. This remains a platform-validation gap, not a reason to stop independent implementation.

Presentation checks now distinguish frame preparation from successful surface presentation. `GpuApplication::presented` (and the UI adapter equivalent) acknowledges a successful WGPU submit/present, never a deferred acquisition; it does not claim physical display completion. `GpuPresenter::present_with` acquires first and does not call application visual preparation for suspended, zero-sized, occluded or otherwise deferred surfaces. Winit uses this path and backs off deferred acquisitions. `HostRequest::Fail` reports fatal update/input errors without waiting for another drawable; the native player test covers a failed navigation while presentation is unavailable. All rewrite smoke examples now count acknowledged presentations and fail at a bounded deadline rather than passing on paint-list counts or hanging.

This exposed an evidence error in earlier checkpoints: their Winit smoke counters measured prepared paint lists, and therefore did not demonstrate desktop-window presentation while the Mac was locked. The prominent correction near the beginning of this document supersedes those earlier claims. `/private/tmp/eldiron-text-target-window.log` correctly fails after the deadline with **zero successful surface presentations**. Do not list that invocation as passed. Headless pixel captures and detached CAMetalLayer tests explicitly asserting `Presented` remain valid. The updated foreign-layer fixture verifies two successful preparations/presentations, no preparation or acknowledgement while suspended/zero-sized, then successful recreation and a third acknowledged presentation, with no framebuffer readback.

Both framework native examples and the native player example compile. All four canonical application compatibility builds, browser framework host/iOS renderer compile and all seven independent dependency boundaries passed. ## Balanced graphical control sources checkpoint (2026-11-12)

The shared graphical player coordinator now retains accepted physical control keys in press order. A release that gameplay never accepted produces no action, duplicate presses do not create sources, aliased keys keep their shared movement held until the final source is released, and releasing a newer alias restores the remaining press order. The existing `ClientAction` movement reducer is rebuilt from these sources, preserving its directional/isometric rules. Only changed movement states are submitted; explicit Stop always cancels held sources. Camera convention changes re-reduce current held keys, so changing to an isometric camera immediately updates a held diagonal.

Mouse-held movement controls capture keyboard gameplay until release. The application applies the capture stop before the button's own Forward/etc. action and does not append another Off during the same host-state synchronization. An unaccepted keyboard release cannot stop that mouse action. `PlayerInputStats` exposes submitted-action, pending-startup and held-source counts without renderer state; startup queue flushing does not recount input. The actual starter integration verifies press/hold/outside-release submission counts, modifier release, modal cancellation and unchanged input statistics across GPU recreation.

Validation: six graphical player/session tests passed, including real starter runtime/device recovery; all 19 non-GPU screen-controller tests passed (the four GPU tests in that particular invocation were not selected); the native player example and all four canonical applications compile. Framework/rendering/dependency code did not change in this checkpoint. The corrected live-Mac validation gap above remains.

## Shared screen focus and keyboard checkpoint (2026-11-12)

Implemented one CPU `ScreenFocus` owner across authored fields, transcript commands, buttons and choices. Stable Tab/Shift-Tab traversal skips hidden, empty, disabled and fully clipped controls; a game screen without UI focus declines Tab for the existing gameplay binding. Active preedit keeps ownership of navigation. Button activation requires a matching Enter/Space release, ignores repeated presses and consumes cancelled releases across focus changes. Movement buttons start on press and stop once on release; pointer takeover and prepare-time hiding stop the former source without replay or a second late-release action. Typed `ScreenCapture` stamps replace the application's capture boolean so programmatic owner changes cancel held movement while GPU/layout recreation preserves it.

Choice activation/navigation uses semantic shared-controller operations without fabricated pointer coordinates. Dropdown selection remains pending until accepted, Tab cancels the popup before traversing, and tabs commit navigation immediately. Blocking transcripts precede focused-button activation. Input eligibility shares finite, positive viewport-intersection rules with the root paint clip; captured drags/releases retain their owner outside it. Focus borders for buttons/choices use authored colors and GPU paint operations, with no CPU screen image.

## Common framework editor adoption checkpoint (2026-11-12)

Native `TheTextLineEdit` fields, including numeric ranges and embedded `TheTreeItem` fields, now use the same retained `EditorView`/`EditorController` as game fields and transcript commands. Legacy text values remain a compatibility projection for existing widget APIs and the explicit CPU reference path; native editing/selection/preedit/history and GPU paint no longer use the legacy cursor/draw implementation. External value/document replacement creates a new callback epoch even for identical text, while ordinary layout/font/GPU changes preserve it. Added semantic `EditorCommand` operations for menus and shortcuts, shared asynchronous host clipboard routing, explicit blur notification, and visible-layout traversal for editor focus. Tab/Shift-Tab preserves modifiers across focus changes; preedit keeps Tab. Context menus, overlays, hidden stack/tab/shared-layout branches and collapsed tree branches suspend the editor's input scope and cancel preedit/pending clipboard. Callback identity rotates before returning to that editor. Native editor scopes, widget input/state ports and the existing generic host remain separate from the GPU surface; no native text widget accesses the platform clipboard directly.

Numeric drags use grouped neutral-editor transactions: many samples produce one undo entry, release commits one noncontinuous callback, and scope loss cancels the unfinished gesture (restoring live callbacks for continuous fields). A queued blur cannot project an old gesture over a newer external value. Clipboard Copy supersedes earlier Cut/Paste requests so late completions cannot edit; AltGr physical letters do not trigger editor shortcuts before committed text.

## Native code-editor paint foundation (2026-11-12)

Added paint-only syntax colors over the common editor's existing shaped glyphs. The small documented Parley `positioned_glyphs_with_clusters` iterator exposes original UTF-8 cluster ranges while retaining the exact visual/style slice, offsets and baseline of its existing iterator. No shaping/line-breaking/rasterization algorithm changed. Isolated patch/provenance: `vendor/parley/eldiron-editor-glyph-clusters.patch` and `vendor/parley/ELDIRON-PATCH.md`.

`TextLayout::colorized_runs` preserves every glyph/font/position and resolves overlapping spans with last-span precedence. Normalized intervals plus binary lookup avoid a glyph-by-syntax-token quadratic scan. An intersected shaped cluster keeps one color as a unit. `EditorView::paint_decorated` caches immutable annotated runs by editor snapshot and annotation identity, reusing them across caret/layout paints. Search backgrounds, diagnostic underlines, whole-line debug backgrounds and whitespace markers use the same text geometry. Indexed visible-line lookup skips the off-screen prefix with binary search and returns only viewport line metadata; explicit viewport scrolling does not reshape the document. This is not yet full document/glyph virtualization or incremental editing.

## Neutral code-editing policy and saved-state compatibility (2026-11-12)

Added `EditorPolicy`/`EditorTab` and renderer-independent UTF-8 structural edit plans. Newline insertion retains the current CRLF/LF convention and optional leading indentation. Code Tab/Shift-Tab supports spaces, multiline selection, backward Unicode selection and the existing previous-tab-stop outdent behavior; a selection ending at the next line's start excludes that terminal line. Configured Tab width is bounded to 1–256 spaces. Optional bracket completion wraps selected text in one undo transaction; explicit paste and IME composition commits remain literal. Default field/transcript policy remains focus traversal without bracket/indent behavior.

Readonly transitions cancel preedit, unfinished edit groups and pending clipboard requests, rotate the native callback epoch, and retain committed content, selection/copy/navigation and earlier history. They reject mutation/undo/paste until editing resumes, and expose no insertion caret/IME candidate. Starting composition closes a pending user-edit group before taking its own snapshot. Empty clipboard text preserves the document/selection.

The common controller can import/export the existing `TextEditState` JSON schema, including per-row grapheme cursor/selection indices, backward selection direction, CRLF rows and existing options. Export uses committed preedit state; import bounds malformed positions and starts a new document/input epoch/history. This is a compatibility projection: native full bidi affinity and undo remain owned by the retained controller, not serialized into the legacy schema. Creator document services must retain their native editor objects rather than repeatedly replacing them through this adapter.

Verification: 50 text-only tests pass (`/private/tmp/eldiron-code-policy-state-core.log`); 132 UI-enabled library tests and 9 native field integration tests pass (`/private/tmp/eldiron-code-policy-framework.log`); 25 CPU native screen tests pass, with 5 GPU-only cases deliberately excluded (`/private/tmp/eldiron-code-policy-screen.log`). Tests include CRLF indentation/atomic undo, Unicode reversed indent/bracket selection, paste versus typed brackets, readonly recovery/copy, exact saved JSON roundtrip and committed preedit state. ### Selected-text drag moves use the shared editor

The native multiline widget now preserves selected-text drag moves through the common `EditorView` and controller. A press inside the painted selection keeps it intact until release; a three-logical-pixel threshold distinguishes a move from an ordinary click. The drop uses the release position, supports backward Unicode selections, and is a single undoable document transaction without touching the system clipboard. Escape, scope loss, a changed selection or a replaced/edited document cancels the pending gesture. Drop hits carry their document/focus/edit identity, while ordinary font or GPU changes do not invalidate document positions. Native mouse release now projects the changed text/selection into the existing saved state and emits the normal continuous value callback exactly once.

### Source-image retention and complete-frame pinning (2026-11-12)

The UI source-image cache now retains superseded versions until the complete application paint list is known. `PaintList::image_handles` includes ordinary images, filtered images, image outlines and image meshes, including nested opacity/clip scopes. `UiApplicationAdapter` finalizes once after the application's full frame callback, so independent UI/viewport/overlay contributors may safely refer to different versions of the same source in one frame. Individual UI subtrees do not retire resources. Finalization validates scopes and residency before changing cache state; rejected lists leave residency intact.

Default retention targets are 64 MiB of normalized RGBA16F texels and 512 images. LRU eviction applies to unreferenced entries; retained lists pin sources even without new image requests. Superseded unreferenced versions retire immediately at that boundary. An active frame larger than the retention target stays valid and reports its pinned working set/over-budget status; this is explicitly a retention budget, **not a hard cap on all GPU memory or transient frame preparation**. Statistics expose source hits/uploads, retirement, resident texel bytes and pinned working sets. Dimension changes invalidate obsolete textures even when the producer did not set its content-change flag. Explicit teardown clears resources; registry replacement resets only device-domain cache state.

Offscreen callers using `UiImages`/`UiFrameImages` directly must call `finish_frame` with the final combined list before rendering. Finalize a newer frame only after encoding/submitting the prior frame, or include the prior frame's references; independently queued not-yet-encoded frames still require explicit leases. Completed WGPU submissions retain their own bindings/resources. General scene/glyph/scratch budgets, global working-set admission, batching and independently queued-frame leases remain separate work.

### Native graph widget/controller binding (2026-11-12)

`TheGraphView` binds an explicitly application-retained `Arc<Mutex<GraphViewState>>` to native TheUI paint and input ports. This is per-view CPU authoring state (graph/controller/draft), not a GPU/global application owner. Do not share one transient controller between distinct visible views or hold its guard across UI callbacks. The widget's graph painting, shaped text, pointer gestures, native candidate position, clipboard, local text undo and scope lifecycle use the same controller. Source-image handles remain an injected resource map; GPU/device/surface ownership stays outside the widget. No raster graph/font cache or CPU canvas is allocated; invoking the legacy draw adapter is an explicit error.

Applications receive typed `GraphCommitted` events containing reversible edits and a unique document binding token. They apply those edits to their authoritative document/undo owner; they must not persist the whole working graph mid-gesture. This matters when clicking a slider commits the previous text draft: the earlier event must not absorb the new slider's unfinished value. Replacing an authoring document always changes the binding token, including identical content/IDs, so application adapters can reject queued events from an older project/branch. `GraphCommand` keeps graph-level actions with the application rather than falling into the OS text clipboard. Internal text capabilities are advertised while an inline field is active.

Graph canvas keyboard/capture scope remains active even without a text field. Suspended scope/focus loss cancels unfinished pointer gestures; ordinary numeric drags retain capture and commit once. `GraphEditor::cancel_gesture` separates that cancellation from text-draft cancellation, allowing menus to suspend native text composition while preserving committed draft content for resumption. External CPU model edits invalidate paint, and an unchanged widget settles to idle.

### Ordered graph ownership and non-destructive save checkpoints (2026-11-12)

Graph commits now carry a document binding plus a monotonic serial. The CPU view model retains an ordered queue until the application acknowledges an applied prefix. UI wake-up notifications and the queue share immutable `Arc<GraphCommit>` payloads, avoiding copies of node/list values per listener. Applications can lease `pending_through(serial)` outside the model lock, apply transactions to the authoritative project, then acknowledge them. Invalid bindings, future serials and regressing acknowledgements are rejected. Replacing a document clears its queue and changes the binding, preventing old notifications from applying to a new project with matching authored IDs.

`GraphEditor::checkpoint_text` records the current committed draft as a reversible row/list transaction and advances its baseline **without ending focus**. `GraphViewState::checkpoint_text` publishes it for a Save/Play barrier. This preserves Parley preedit, the native callback token, selection and local undo; uncommitted composition and unrelated unfinished pointer gestures are not serialized as completed edits. Repeated checkpoints produce no duplicate edit. A later queued wake-up for an acknowledged serial finds no pending work, so Save cannot create duplicate document undo entries.

Evidence: renderer-free checks pass (145 library, 9 graph-text and 6 graph-widget workflows). The new save-barrier workflow leaves an earlier wake-up queued, leases/applies two ordered transactions, exercises invalid/partial/idempotent acknowledgement, and proves composition still owns Enter after checkpoint. The same composition subsequently commits, local undo survives, and a new checkpoint reverses against the saved baseline. Identical-ID replacement invalidates the old acknowledgement domain. Both explicit native graph GPU-replacement tests still pass; 30 CPU reference graph tests pass; all four applications with Creator native-render compile. Logs: `/private/tmp/eldiron-native-graph-checkpoint-{framework,neutral,gpu,reference,apps}.log`.

Creator has not adopted this barrier yet. Its prefab adapter must consume only the addressed prefix during ordinary event handling, collect/checkpoint pending drafts before Save/branch/session transitions, and route committed notifications to their owner even after the active dock changes. Authoring validation failures and per-project draft persistence need explicit treatment. Queue acknowledgement is an application responsibility; full pending-command memory/backpressure limits remain part of the outstanding application/resource acceptance work.


### Creator native prefab ownership and authoring barriers (2026-11-12)

The prefab pane now binds an application-retained native `GraphViewState` through `TheGraphView` when command painting is enabled. It consumes only the addressed, ordered commit prefix and acknowledges adopted drafts. Ordinary renders do not rebase a live text draft from the last compiled project. Real source/branch/project replacement changes the binding, rejecting stale text callbacks, queued graph commits and drops. Graph drops carry the graph coordinates captured at input time; later camera movement cannot relocate a queued drop. Native gesture-start signals let the source owner stop its existing preview without replaying the legacy graph pointer controller.

Creator Save, Save As completion, Play and non-discard project transitions now collect dock-owned completed drafts, including hidden docks. Checkpointing preserves preedit, text callback identity, selection and local undo; delayed UI wake-ups do not apply a transaction twice. Numeric prefab compilation errors keep the invalid draft and diagnostic, leave compiled geometry unchanged, and block Save/Play/source transitions until corrected or explicitly discarded through the existing close flow. Independent valid dock commits still apply if another dock reports an error. These are product validation outcomes, not agent permission prompts.

The CPU prefab store no longer constructs `RUSTERIX` or `SCENEMANAGER` just to synchronize an authoring edit: it updates derived CPU placements and only contacts already assembled presentation owners. ### Asset-scoped prefab graph transactions (2026-11-12)

Prefab graph authoring now emits a CPU `shared::prefab_graph::PrefabGraphChange` rather than cloning the whole project into undo. One transaction retains only the target asset and its optional graph source before/after the compiled edit. Applying/undoing/redoing preserves unrelated project metadata, other assets and current world edits. Same-asset edits remain ordered by their authoring owner; this is not a concurrent merge protocol for independent edits to the same asset. Wrong candidate identities are rejected; stale transactions do not resurrect removed targets; repeated application of the same state is a no-op. Undo restores graph-source absence as well as presence, keeping existing project serialization semantics.

Derived attachment updates live in `sync_prefab_placements`, separate from UI and presentation. Restoring an asset rederives item and prop transforms from current placements, instead of restoring obsolete region snapshots. Creator's `PrefabGraphEdit` undo atom uses that transaction and only then synchronizes already assembled legacy presentation owners through a separate adapter. It sends the existing prefab projection refresh; no full scene rebuild or renderer creation is required for this atom. Native source replacement also clears obsolete compilation diagnostics and rejects the old text epoch, including a valid external undo while an invalid draft was retained.

### Stable graph cell addresses and complete fold transactions (2026-11-12)

Preparing NodesDock adoption exposed an ownership hole: a list text focus stored only numeric row/column positions. Focus now captures authored row and column identities and resolves their current positions for input, paint, IME geometry, checkpoint and cancellation. Reordering identified rows/columns preserves the same native callback token, preedit, selection and local undo. The resulting reversible transaction restores only the intended cell within the current row value, retaining other current fields. Removed/type-replaced/ambiguous cells revoke the target, rejecting stale IME commits and pending clipboard results instead of modifying a replacement at the old index. The renderer-independent reference input path uses the same resolution.

Legacy tables without unambiguous row/column identities keep working and serialize without invented row IDs. They retain one transient shared table guard while focused; an external change to other cells/structure conservatively revokes that focus. This has an explicit per-focused-table snapshot cost; it is not a completed global document/history-memory bound. Native paint resolves the focused address once per list, avoiding a new lookup/guard scan for every painted cell.

The same completed-edit audit found node folding mutated the working graph without emitting an edit. Fold/unfold now produce reversible node replacements, so the native ordered consumer persists authored fold state. Explicit reference prefab stores also drain their controller's completed edit payloads instead of retaining a second unused queue beside the asset undo owner.

### Atomic branch transitions and editing-session history (2026-11-12)

Added a CPU-only `NodeSourceTransaction` port for completed domain operations and source-local undo/redo. A transaction patches explicit source slots against their expected canonical documents, validates all candidates before publication, and writes the current owner envelope once. Promoting a nonempty unrooted draft to a new branch clears the draft and installs that branch in one operation; undo removes the root and restores the draft with its original node/row/port identities and exact authored text. Current unrelated branches and Project fields are retained. Occupied destinations, removed owners, changed source, unsupported versions, multiple roots in a single branch slot and inconsistent source addresses reject without partial Project/source/binding updates. Raw invalid configuration source remains saveable while generated data is replaced only after successful compilation.

History records the effective private layout/schema baseline as the state to undo to, while forward publication still compares the stored canonical baseline. Undo/redo refresh the written side of the transaction with the actual current schema projection, so a later redo can compare the source that undo actually published. Source-slot branch positions retain relative neighboring identities and a fallback index; restoring a removed branch preserves the positions of newer unrelated siblings instead of restoring an owner-wide order snapshot. These transaction/position records are ephemeral authoring data, with no project format change. A no-op does not materialize absent authoring source, alter generated entity data, revoke bindings or erase redo.

`NativeNodesWorkspace` now owns one history stack and stable editing-session identity per retained source view. Completed UI packets record source-local history. Completed domain edits can move that same session and its undo stack between draft/root addresses. The corresponding native model/panel controllers and widget identity are replaced; an old widget holding retired Arcs cannot start authoring the replacement source. Viewport and surviving selection are retained, old IME/clipboard scopes are revoked, and hidden-source operations do not redirect the visible owner. Deleted-branch sessions remain reachable for undo across owner switches; clean external source rebases create a new session/history epoch. Failed history comparisons keep the cursor and current source intact. An independent live destination editor cannot be stolen even when its canonical draft is empty.

### Application-owned audio, source publication and recovery (2026-11-12)

Added `rusterix::audio::output::AudioOutput` with an injected device factory and explicit source revisions/presentation elapsed time. It owns desired looping voices, bus volumes, bounded cache state, lazy device creation, diagnostics and device retry backoff outside the window/GPU/view lifetime. Each incoming command is delivered once. Missing/unready devices drop one-shots rather than replaying stale effects later; recovery restores desired loops and bus volumes once. Suspend/resume preserves existing voices without generating new Play commands. Stop clears desired playback; document reset additionally revokes clip caches and project bus state while retaining a healthy device. Default cache/voice/bus/PCM limits are provisional guardrails, not measured release budgets.

`AudioServices` composes this owner with other common-player services. Borrowed `RegionOutputs` fan out the original session payloads; the audio owner forwards only non-audio slices to the inner service. CPU advance, user gestures and host suspend/resume have explicit service hooks; frame painting and GPU recreation do not pump or replace audio. The native example uses this service. Canonical launcher/Creator Play adoption is still pending. Shared CPU startup now publishes imported WAV/OGG bytes as well as generated FX source without a device/font registry or project mutation. Region snapshots omit raw imported playback bytes while the outward source registry retains them; workers emit named commands.

The real engine decodes WAV/OGG into bounded streaming mono PCM without first building a second full interleaved buffer. Resident accounting deduplicates shared PCM and counts buffers pinned by active voices after cache eviction. Generated FX sizes use checked arithmetic before synthesis allocation. Source invalidation fingerprints each normalized FX definition: unrelated effects/formatting/defaults/metadata and shadowed imports cannot restart music. Changed sources restart only their own looping voices. Added a small generated stereo Vorbis fixture for actual OGG decoding, so codec coverage does not depend on an output device or ffmpeg at runtime.

Actual mixer regressions exposed a silent sample at loop boundaries and lost long-track position precision after 2^24 frames. Boundary interpolation now wraps before sampling; playback positions use f64 while PCM remains f32. Mixer sampling no longer clones the bus-volume map per sample. New invalidation/oversized-gap regressions also failed before their fixes (log `/private/tmp/eldiron-native-audio-fx-invalidation-red.log`); the oversized single-repeat gap previously overflowed the synthesizer stride even though the total-length guard passed. Browser builds previously lacked CPAL's WebAudio feature; that target feature is now enabled explicitly. Browser unlock/suspend/resume acts on the existing AudioContext, consuming promise results, rather than repeatedly invoking CPAL play (which schedules its callback pump).

### Cancellable native audio preparation and independent service scheduling (2026-11-12)

The audio device boundary now installs immutable `PreparedClip` PCM. Native `AudioOutput` defaults to a lazy CPU worker, admitting only one preparation job/completion at a time. The host polls completions during application command/update processing; no codec or synthesis runs from screen painting or device installation. WAV/OGG decoding and FX synthesis check cancellation periodically. Direct generated PCM retains the reference 16-bit quantization exactly while avoiding an intermediate WAV allocation/decoding pass. Prepared data is shared with mixer voices through Arc; installation still checks resident cached/active PCM before publishing.

Preparation requests have monotonic identities independent of document/content revision and GPU generations. Source replacement, Stop, bus clearing when no other voice needs the source, document reset, expired one-shots and owner drop revoke pending work. Completed results are accepted only for the still-current cache request, so a codec that ignores cancellation cannot publish into a replacement document. Device recovery discards pending one-shots/preparations while retaining desired loops. A bounded queue permits fresh one-shots to await cold decoding; expiry, suspend, missing/unready device and source replacement drop them. One-shots are never replayed after recovery. Defaults currently admit 32 pending one-shots with 250 ms lifetime, 64 MiB source/decoded preparation caps and one in-flight job. These are provisional guardrails; release performance is not yet verified. Runtime imported sources now use immutable Arc byte storage. CPU publication reuses unchanged storage, asset clones retain the same source, and submitting a job clones only its Arc. Project serialization still owns the original authored bytes. FX jobs carry normalized definitions instead of a source-document copy/TOML parse. Temporary preparation remains bounded separately from resident device PCM; Vec-to-Arc conversion can briefly retain both PCM allocations, so the configured preparation cap is not a claim of total process peak memory.

The deterministic adapter lets lifecycle tests hold real CPU preparation jobs and deliver arbitrarily late results. **24 audio cases pass**, including actual threaded generated/Vorbis decoding, native default-preparer/output integration, exact reference quantization, stale source/document completion rejection, bounded queue age/count, no stale one-shot replay, shared-source bus cancellation and close cancellation. Final development-test log `/private/tmp/eldiron-native-audio-preparation-verified.log`; release performance remains unverified. The first broader pass also verified six common-player cases, 15 independent runtime/terminal cases, 118 reference-client cases (six pre-existing ignored), native example, CPU browser runtime, player browser/iOS simulator, all four applications and all seven renderer boundaries (`/private/tmp/eldiron-native-audio-preparation-{player,headless,reference,cpu-web,web,ios,host,apps,boundaries}.log`). After immutable source and independent service wakeup changes, the **seven common-player cases**, the source-publication and region-snapshot cases, **15 runtime/terminal cases**, **118 reference-client cases** (six pre-existing ignored), native example, isolated CPU browser runtime, player browser/iOS simulator, all four applications and all seven renderer boundaries pass. ### Runtime-bound screen services and per-view relative mouse look (2026-11-12)

Closed the retained-service restart gap identified above. The screen binds its runtime incarnation before addressed event delivery, frame preparation or UI routing. A changed incarnation revokes transcript messages/queued choices/pause state/command drafts, focus and editor/IME identities, clipboard ownership, pending control gestures, retained content sources and view configuration. Authored control configuration and input bindings remain available. Binding before `receive` preserves a new batch delivered before the first new frame; repeated preparation cannot clear it. Painting/preparing scene views against a different runtime without screen preparation returns an explicit error. This is lifecycle handling for a retained authored screen, not an API for recompiling changed screen definitions from a different project.

Speech and private world-description overlays also bind their own runtime identities, including when moved to a newly constructed screen during navigation. Font publication checks `(runtime incarnation, content revision)` and fingerprints raw font bytes: unchanged fonts keep their blob/glyph identities, while different bytes under reused authored IDs/revisions rebuild the registry. GPU recreation retains the same runtime incarnation and preserves live messages/passages. The common player revokes pending host clipboard requests and held controls on a runtime change before its clipboard-result fast path can deliver an old result.

Four focused regressions originally all failed (`/private/tmp/eldiron-native-screen-restart-red.log`) and now pass: input before the first new frame, stale IME/clipboard and dialog ownership, fresh transcript delivery surviving first preparation, moved overlays, unchanged GPU-recovery message identities and changed font bytes under unchanged content revision. The assembled CPU-only player case additionally stops the actual starter runtime with a clipboard request in flight and rejects its result before any new frame.

Relative first-person look is a separate view-bound input service inside the acknowledged world owner. It shares `rusterix::camera::mouse_look::MouseLook` with the reference client and emits `LookYaw` through the CPU session; vertical pitch belongs to the individual game widget and reaches that view's next prepared camera. Published mouse sensitivity/inversion settings, the displayed view rectangle/mode, runtime player, source binding and UI occlusion determine eligibility. Looking at empty sky needs no geometry hit, GPU readback or color picking buffer. Switching views retains each view's own pitch. Hidden/moved/rebound/modal/unfocused/stale views, pointer leave and Escape revoke look. A changed setting waits for its own presentation acknowledgement. Absolute pointer positions and precise scroll retain the existing inverse viewport mapping; raw relative device deltas retain their host units so letterboxing/window size cannot change look sensitivity. Review of the reference client's direct `client_mouse_motion(dx, dy)` path caught the earlier viewport-scaling mismatch before commit. The shared CPU policy also rejects sensitivity multiplication overflow before it can corrupt facing or emit a non-finite yaw.

The initial mouse-look fixtures omitted the runtime player marker; one GPU fixture also still selected the non-mouse camera mode. Those fixtures were corrected without weakening the assertions (`/private/tmp/eldiron-native-mouse-look-focused.log`); **all 11 pointer/look owner cases including the actual GPU ray view pass** (`/private/tmp/eldiron-native-mouse-look-focused-fixed.log`). The assembled GPU fixture additionally sends host relative motion before/after acknowledgement, verifies exactly one CPU submission, checks pitch and a changed prepared camera matrix, and verifies no added readback. The final 42-case screen suite, CPU browser runtime, native-player browser/iOS simulator, native window example, all four application checks and all seven renderer boundaries pass (`/private/tmp/eldiron-native-screen-services-{screen-final,cpu-web,web,ios,host,apps,boundaries}.log`). ### Resolved artwork descriptors and animation-phase cache ownership (2026-11-12)

Split source selection from materialization. `PixelSource::resolve_tile` returns a borrowed authored tile or a small synthetic noise/palette descriptor; `ResolvedTile::frame_texture` borrows the selected authored texture. Metadata lookup does not clone a tile's texture array or generate synthetic pixel buffers. The existing `tile_from_tile_list` materialization API delegates to the same resolver, preserving legacy callers and source priority. Tokens distinguish the actual borrowed asset and its `Tile::frame_index`, including the separation of spatial UV pages from animation phases. Synthetic palette/noise descriptors are stable across presentation frames. These tokens are ephemeral cache identities; the independent asset publication/content revision remains required.

`ContentRecipe::resolve` now produces a `ResolvedContent` plan before `ContentSources` decides whether to build pixels. Item/portrait/profile source selection, project-icon priority, frame selection and square-icon fitting share metadata helpers with reference drawing. Existing source pixels are cloned only when materialization is needed; square fitting and synthetic/generated art also run on cache misses. The selected source/phase replaces absolute clock frame numbers in presentation cache keys. Missing artwork is memoized across advancing frames. The conservative public recipe fingerprint remains available, while concrete-source caches use the resolved fingerprint.

Bitmap avatar plans track the resolved perspective/body frame and independent equipped-tile phases. Hidden weapon animation cannot churn an unchanged body source. Procedural `ResolvedSprite` plans retain immutable compiled geometry, quantized/clamped pose, surface-material phases, yaw and joint selection. Both native source preparation and existing sprite APIs use this same selected plan. A late compiled-variant publication cannot swap the source between cache lookup and materialization. Resolution does not rasterize the selected sprite; materialization first checks the existing sprite cache. Cold geometry/material compilation and variant preparation retain their existing owners and are not claimed to have zero startup cost. Static procedural geometry without a motion clip now uses one pose key while retaining independent animated-material keys. Non-aligned loops, completed non-looping clips, material playback and supplied joint poses retain their existing semantics.

The initial descriptor pass preserved all six existing source cases. New regressions then proved tiled/item phase reuse but failed bitmap-avatar reuse (`/private/tmp/eldiron-native-source-resolution-phase-red-fixed.log`); resolved avatar plans close that gap. The first new fixtures used the wrong AvatarWidget frame field and omitted UV-page fields (`/private/tmp/eldiron-native-source-resolution-phase-red.log`); those setup errors were corrected before interpreting the cache failure. A subsequent compile caught removal of the materializing item-tile helper still used by D2/D3 scene builders; that adapter was restored on top of the shared descriptor resolver (`/private/tmp/eldiron-native-source-resolution-sources.log`). No scene-builder compatibility caller was silently dropped.

Verified **nine CPU artwork cases**, **18 procedural-avatar cases**, **three avatar-builder cases** and **119 reference-client cases** (six pre-existing ignored), including equipped animation, missing assets, source priority, bounded cache leases, static/noise art, bitmap phases, non-aligned procedural loops, material animation, completed poses, and retained compiled selection (`/private/tmp/eldiron-native-source-resolution-{sources-fixed,procedural,avatar,reference}.log`). The retained-sample test resolves without filling the sprite cache, clears the current compiled-cache publication, then materializes from the retained sample without recompilation. This is fault-injection evidence for that source boundary, not complete application-wide async-job acceptance.

The native world drag fixture now advances presentation frames while checking unchanged static-source build counts. ## Asynchronous native material diagnostics checkpoint (2026-11-12)

Native geometry now consumes MaterialZ's existing four-byte GPU status buffer
asynchronously before publishing a procedural frame. Completion callbacks send
readiness only; the owning cache reads/unmaps the status on its own thread.
Superseded source maps are cancelled, delayed receipts are ignored by ID, and
dropping a cache cancels outstanding maps. The existing MaterialZ error decoder
is shared without changing source or serialized representations. No displayed
color/viewport buffer is mapped; status bytes are tracked separately.

A pending output retains its immutable GPU image lease until diagnostics finish.
Creator schedules another frame while waiting. Failure retains the last valid
paint and its actual presentation token, reports a deduplicated status, and keeps
the application running; subsequent valid sources recover. Bounds and device
replacement continue to follow the shared host contract.

## Procedural HUD GPU source conversion (after 8cd7b48c, in progress)

Previous goal turn made verified progress at **8cd7b48c** (paint/props commands,
staged actions, shared bundled font fallback). Current work closes the identified
Color/Noise CPU thumbnail producer adapter; full main viewport cutover is still

`editor_overlay::procedural::ProceduralIcon` now retains only original source
parameters, the three legacy Color noise properties and logical source size.
Native HUD preparation selects source descriptors, borrows the first authored
tile/material frame, or imports a single palette source texel. It does not clone
whole Tile/RME/UV arrays or invoke `PixelSource::to_tile`. The retained helper is
explicitly named `get_icon_reference`; reference pixels are generated only by the
reference adapter/export consumer. Existing source precedence and light flags
remain. Core PixelSource algorithms and all serialized project shapes are
unchanged.

`GpuIcons` receives the application's explicit GpuContext and image registry.
A GPU render pass generates RGBA8 sRGB/straight source textures from a **96-byte
uniform parameter block**. Color noise/pixelization, RGB/hue/luminance and both
value/voronoi NoiseMaterial modes are ported to WGSL, preserving original byte
quantization, signed fract semantics and even the legacy hue-unit convention.
The source is then blitted through the common PixelImage compositor. There is
no procedural CPU bitmap upload, implicit output readback, window or separate
GPU initialization. Swash text remains on the common atlas path.

`OverlayImages` is the application-owned resource interface: an injected
`IconFrameImages` forwards ordinary source assets through the common bounded UI
cache and resolves procedural descriptors on the same registry/device. A sink
without the injected producer returns an explicit error; no CPU fallback is
hidden in native paint. Main world/tool integration must install this resource
adapter and finalize both caches against the assembled root list.

The procedural cache retains immutable versions by shader parameter identity,
tracks bytes/entries/builds/hits/evictions/pinned bytes, retires only unpinned
sources at complete-root finalization, and reports an over-budget pinned working
set without destroying live paint. Registry/device ownership is checked;
replacement registries cannot remove foreign source handles. CPU descriptions
survive GPU recreation. Warm frames reuse source textures; idle finalization
avoids sorting retirement candidates unless actually over budget.

DPR validation note:
- Consulted the primary Resize Observer draft's device-pixel box contract:
  https://drafts.csswg.org/resize-observer/#resize-observer-interface
  It describes device-pixel-content-box and implementation-specific pixel
  snapping, rather than requiring an app-side CSS-size multiplication. The
  measured25% discrepancy is larger than rounding; CDP-only metrics are not
  enough to establish actual monitor-density behavior. Retain this as an open
  browser/physical-DPR check, not a passed gate or a production sizing change.
  Protocol reference: https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Emulation/
- Delayed game start/world rendering and CSS resize are independently verified;
  a bounded actual-device destroy/recreation probe is running on the existing
  game session, without the unresolved fractional emulation step blocking it.

M9 versioned Creator/byte-document batch (continuation, not a completion gate):
- Added v1 ABI/version negotiation and monotonic host handles around the common
  ForeignApplicationHost. All Swift Creator input, lifecycle, text, clipboard,
  menu and theme calls now carry their owning Renderer handle. A destroyed host
  cannot receive a stale callback after recreation. A second active Creator is
  explicitly rejected pending M5 global retirement; this is not multiwindow
  ownership. Legacy exports remain compatible; only create_v1 opts into native
  document host requests.
- The host consumes Open/Save/Save As requests from toolbar/key/controller paths
  as well as macOS menus. Requests carry the active ephemeral document identity.
  Swift macOS panels capture it before yielding, read/write bytes off the main
  thread, and reject completions for another host or active tab. iOS now has
  UIDocumentPicker open/export/cancel routing, retaining immutable export bytes
  and retiring temporary files on completion/teardown. Both wrappers compile;
  actual physical panels/mobile execution are not yet verified.
- Document loads decode with existing migrations before replacement, retire
  native output bindings only on success, and distinguish untitled loaded bytes
  from templates so starter assets are not silently injected. Clean replacement
  commits buffered authoring edits before rechecking the dirty guard. Invalid
  data/UUID/stale-host/stale-document/canceled save cannot replace/clean a tab.
- Save tickets own immutable encoded bytes, copied into caller-owned memory.
  Size queries and undersized-buffer behavior are documented in Bridge.h. A
  pending save is bounded to one snapshot and is canceled on its document close
  or replacement. Successful completion can address an inactive source tab.
- First assembled native check exposed document_info using the all-tabs dirty

  integration then passed1 test/121.34s, including byte decode/failure, busy/
  canceled/wrong/duplicate tickets, actual write/re-read, unchanged save, tab
  switch/old completion and zero additional GPU readback. Log:
  /private/tmp/eldiron-native-document-io-final-metal.log.
- Actual Swift/static-library check found a distinct archive comparison bug:
  ZIP FileOptions uses current timestamps when its time feature is active, so
  identical documents can encode different container bytes across seconds. Save
  completion now compares canonical serialized *authored source*, retaining full
  bytes without a collision-prone hash; it excludes ZIP metadata and projections
  refreshed on the encoder's clone. Archive encoding/schema is unchanged. This
  replaces the earlier in-progress claim of comparing exact encoded archives.
  It also avoids a second archive compression at completion, but snapshot memory
  (archive + canonical source + host copy) still needs M0/M2 budget measurement.
